claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and any children you're enquiring about.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?** If so, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have one child - my son Alex, he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm assessing eligibility for your son Alex, who is 8 years old.

Before I proceed with my assessment, let me first read the official eligibility criteria to ensure I'm applying the correct rules.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, I've reviewed the eligibility criteria. Now I need to ask you some questions to determine your specific circumstances. Let me start:

**Do you live with Alex in the UK, or does he live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful information.

Now I need to ask about your immigration status to ensure you meet the residency requirements:

**What is your immigration status in the UK? For example, are you a British citizen, do you have settled status, pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or another visa status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen, born and raised here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that information. That's straightforward.

Now I have one more important question to ensure there are no complications with Alex's eligibility:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, residential care, or any form of formal care arrangement? Or is he living with you full-time at home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. He's living with me full-time at home. He goes to school during the day and comes home every evening.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that information. I now have all the details I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided and the official eligibility criteria, let me provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Excellent news!** You are eligible for Child Benefit for your son Alex.

**Summary of why Alex qualifies:**
- He is under 16 years old
- You live with him in the UK and are responsible for him
- You are a British citizen with the right to reside in the UK
- He is living at home with you full-time and is not in any care arrangement that would affect eligibility

You can now proceed to make a claim for Child Benefit. If you have any other questions or need further assistance, please feel free to ask!
